original_question: For actions (C, G) satisfying condition (N), describe the possible values of |G|/g_C^2 and, for each such value, bound the dimension of the corresponding subvariety of M_g parametrizing curves with that kind of big p-group action.
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.2, Question 6.12 (with notation and scope supplied by Definition 6.2 and Proposition 6.3).
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact two-part task asked in the paper: determine the possible values of the numerical invariant |G|/g_C^2, and for each such value bound the dimension of the corresponding locus in M_g. It also correctly ties the problem to actions satisfying condition (N), i.e. the paper’s big p-group actions.
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated: k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0.
The curve should be specified as a nonsingular projective curve C over k.
G should be specified as a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C).
Condition (N) should be spelled out explicitly: g_C>0 and |G|/g_C > 2p/(p-1).
Because the question is phrased in terms of M_g, one should make explicit that g=g_C and that one is considering the moduli space of smooth genus-g curves, hence implicitly g_C>=2.
The moduli-theoretic locus should be phrased paper-faithfully as the subvariety of M_g corresponding to curves C admitting such a big action, rather than a moduli space of actions themselves.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, let C be a nonsingular projective curve over k of genus g_C=g>=2, and let G be a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C) such that (C,G) satisfies Nakajima’s condition (N), namely g_C>0 and |G|/g_C>2p/(p-1). Describe the set of values attained by the quotient |G|/g_C^2 for such pairs (C,G), and for each attained value give an upper bound for the dimension of the subvariety of M_g consisting of curves C that admit such a big p-group action.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it matches Question 6.12 almost verbatim. To make it stand alone, the main additions are the ground field, the smooth projective nature of C, the requirement that G be a finite p-subgroup of Aut_k(C), and the explicit inequality defining condition (N) from Definition 6.2. Proposition 6.3 supplies the nearby structural context for pairs satisfying (N), showing that this is the intended class of big p-group actions. The nearby Theorem 6.7 and Questions 6.5–6.11 show that the paper is studying strong structural restrictions on such actions, but the draft specifically targets the numerical-moduli question posed in Question 6.12, not the neighboring classification questions about G_2.
